newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tamils attack Sri Lankan facilities, eight dead.
newsitem.headline: Tamils attack Sri Lankan facilities, eight dead.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels killed at least eight people in separate attacks on police and facilities controlled by Sri Lankan security forces over 24 hours, military officials said on Thursday.

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), fighting for a separate state for minority Tamils, said many civilians were killed by army shelling while hundreds of others fled to India despite stepped up boat patrols to stop them.
A military spokeman said there had been four attacks and an attempted attack on security forces in the past 24 hours.
"Terrorists simultaneously blasted the Mannar power station and telecommunications tower and fired at policemen who were on duty," he said. Two policemen were killed and two wounded.

Clashes that followed the attack in northwestern Mannar island, off the rebel-controlled territory of the Wanni, also left two more policemen dead, he said. Rebel radio transmissions indicated that one Tamil guerrilla also died, he said.
Early on Thursday, Tamil Tigers also attacked police in the southeastern town of Amparai, killing two police reservists, a guard and a Moslem woman, a military officer said.
Tamil guerrillas, driven by soldiers out of their northern Kilinochchi stronghold, have said they are hitting back at security forces elsewhere.
The guerrillas' Voice of Tigers radio said "the LTTE has intensified attacks on government troops in other areas".

It also said 436 Tamil refugees fleeing the war-ravaged Kilinochchi area arrived in Rameswaram at the southern tip of the Indian subcontinent since the army launched a fresh offensive against the rebels late last month.
"Many civilians were killed...during artillery attacks by the Sri Lankan army in the recent military offensive," an LTTE statement, which was faxed to Reuters, said.
The army has said artillery strikes were on rebel targets.

The army took Kilinochchi, the last major town controlled by the rebels, on Sunday after a week of fierce fighting in which 269 soldiers and more than 700 rebels were killed, according to military statistics.
The LTTE has so far said only 90 of its fighters died. With reporters banned from the war zone, no independent verification was possible.

The rebel radio said about 3,000 Tamil refugees had made the narrow crossing between Sri Lanka and India's Tamil Nadu state since the influx began in July when the army first launched its offensive on Kilinochchi.
